arxiv-1311-3415.title: Influence of substitution on the optical properties of functionalized pentacene monomers and crystals: Experiment and theory
arxiv-1311-3415.creator: Y. Saeed 1 , K. Zhao 1 , N. Singh 1,2 , R. Li 1 , J. E. Anthony 3 , A. Amassian 1 , and U. Schwingenschlögl 1
arxiv-1311-3415.description: Abstract The influence of solubilizing substitutional groups on the electronic and optical properties of functionalized pentacene molecules and crystals have been investigated. Density functional theory is used to calculate the electronic and optical properties of pentacene, TIBS-CF 3 -pentacene, and TIPS-pentacene.

arxiv-2206-10295.title: Dynamic Reserve Price Design for Lazada Sponsored Search DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: 31st ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 17-22, 2022; Atlanta, Georgia, USA Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Information systems Computational advertisin
arxiv-2206-10295.creator: Mang Li
arxiv-2206-10295.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mang Li. In e-commerce platform, users will be less likely to use organic search if sponsored search shows them unexpected advertising items, which will be a hidden cost for the platform. In order to incorporate the hidden cost into auction mechanism which helps create positive growth for the platform, we turn to a reserve price design to decide whether we sell the traffic, as well as build healthy relationships between revenue and user experience.

arxiv-2308-02062.title: Diffusion Models for Counterfactual Generation and Anomaly Detection in Brain Images
arxiv-2308-02062.creator: Alessandro Fontanella, Grant Mair, Joanna Wardlaw, Emanuele Trucco, Amos Storkey
arxiv-2308-02062.description: Abstract Segmentation masks of pathological areas are useful in many medical applications, such as brain tumour and stroke management. Moreover, healthy counterfactuals of diseased images can be used to enhance radiologists’ training files and to improve the interpretability of segmentation models.

arxiv-2312-03147.title: Neural parameter calibration and uncertainty quantification for epidemic forecasting
arxiv-2312-03147.creator: Thomas Gaskin, Tim Conrad, Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Christof Schütte
arxiv-2312-03147.description: Abstract The recent COVID-19 pandemic has thrown the importance of accurately forecasting contagion dynamics and learning infection parameters into sharp focus. At the same time, effective policy-making requires knowledge of the uncertainty on such predictions, in order, for instance, to be able to ready hospitals and intensive care units for a worst-case scenario without needlessly wasting resources.

arxiv-2410-08639.title: Analog simulation of noisy quantum circuits
arxiv-2410-08639.creator: Etienne Granet, Kévin Hémery, Henrik Dreyer
arxiv-2410-08639.description: Abstract It is well-known that simulating quantum circuits with low but non-zero hardware noise is more difficult than without noise. It requires either to perform density matrix simulations (coming with a space overhead) or to sample over “quantum trajectories” where Kraus operators are inserted randomly (coming with a runtime overhead).

arxiv-2501-07721.title: LLMic: Romanian Foundation Language Model
arxiv-2501-07721.creator: Vlad-Andrei Bădoiu, Alexandru M. Gherghescu, Alexandru Agache, Mihai-Valentin Dumitru, Costin Raiciu
arxiv-2501-07721.description: Abstract . Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across various tasks with commercial models leading the way. While open models usually operate at a smaller scale, they maintain competitiveness through specialization and fine-tuning. However, a significant challenge persists: open models often underperform in low-resource languages due to limited representation in the training corpus.

arxiv-2503-23369.title: Asymptotically accurate and geometric locking-free finite element implementation of a refined shell theory
arxiv-2503-23369.creator: Khanh Chau Le a,b and Hoang-Giang Bui c
arxiv-2503-23369.description: Abstract Accurate finite element analysis of refined shell theories is crucial but often hindered by membrane and shear locking effects. While various element-based locking-free techniques exist, this work addresses the problem at the theoretical level by utilizing results from asymptotic analysis.

arxiv-2503-24175.title: What is the Funniest Number? An investigation of numerical humor
arxiv-2503-24175.creator: E. G. Pottebaum Department of Physics, Yale University
arxiv-2503-24175.description: Abstract In a preliminary study of numerical humor, we propose the Perceived Specificity Hypothesis (PSH). The PSH states that, for nonnegative integers < < 100, the funniness of a number increases with its apparent precision. A survey of 68 individuals supports the veracity of this hypothesis and indicates that oddly specific numbers tend to be funniest.

arxiv-2506-22231.title: Adapting University Policies for Generative AI: Opportunities, Challenges, and Policy Solutions in Higher Education
arxiv-2506-22231.creator: Russell Beale
arxiv-2506-22231.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Russell Beale. The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools—especially large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT—has ushered in a transformative era in higher education. Universities in developed regions are increasingly integrating these technologies into research, teaching, and assessment. On one hand, LLMs can enhance productivity by streamlining literature reviews, facilitating idea generation, assisting with coding and data analysis, and even supporting grant proposal drafting. On the other hand, their use raises significant concerns regarding academic integrity, ethical boundaries, and equitable access.

arxiv-2512-19443.title: D²Pruner: Debiased Importance and Structural Diversity for MLLM Token Pruning
arxiv-2512-19443.creator: Evelyn Zhang, Fufu Yu, Aoqi Wu, Zichen Wen, Ke Yan, Shouhong Ding, Biqing Qi, Linfeng Zhang
arxiv-2512-19443.description: Abstract Processing long visual token sequences poses a significant computational burden on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While token pruning offers a path to acceleration, we find that current methods, while adequate for general understanding, catastrophically fail on fine-grained localization tasks.

pmc-11368876.title: Mitigating the risk of inflammatory type primary graft dysfunction by applying an integrated approach to assess, modify and match risk factors in lung transplantation
pmc-11368876.creator: Sue A. Braithwaite, Elize M. Berg, Linda M. de Heer, Jitte Jennekens, Arne Neyrinck, Elise van Hooijdonk, Bart Luijk, Wolfgang F. F. A. Buhre, Niels P. van der Kaaij
pmc-11368876.description: Long-term outcome following lung transplantation remains one of the poorest of all solid organ transplants with a 1- and 5-year survival of 85% and 59% respectively for adult lung transplant recipients and with 50% of patients developing chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) in the first 5 years following transplant.

pmc-11438418.title: Early recurrence as a pivotal event in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: identifying predictors and key molecular signals for survivors
pmc-11438418.creator: Ying Li, Zongwei Huang, Ximing Zeng, Yuhui Pan, Lishui Wu, Jing Wang, Ronghui Chen, Yingjie Xie, Jinghua Lai, Duanyu Lin, Sufang Qiu
pmc-11438418.description: PurposeThe duration of response to treatment is a significant prognostic indicator, with early recurrence (ER) often predicting poorer survival outcomes in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) survivors. This study seeks to elucidate the factors contributing to the onset of ER following radiotherapy in NPC survivors.MethodsThis investigation encompassed 2,789 newly diagnosed NPC patients who underwent radical intensity-modulated radiotherapy.

pmc-11510583.title: NiO Nano- and Microparticles Prepared by Solvothermal Method—Amazing Catalysts for CO2 Methanation
pmc-11510583.creator: Arkadii Bikbashev, Tomáš Stryšovský, Martina Kajabová, Zuzana Kovářová, Robert Prucek, Aleš Panáček, Josef Kašlík, Tamás Fodor, Csaba Cserháti, Zoltán Erdélyi, Libor Kvítek
pmc-11510583.description: Nickel oxide (NiO) is one of the most popular hydrogenation catalysts. In heterogeneous catalysis, nickel oxide is used, for example, as a suitable methanation catalyst in the Fischer–Tropsch reaction not only for CO hydrogenation but also in the modified Fischer–Tropsch reaction with CO2.

pmc-11583309.title: Autochthonous dengue outbreak in Marche Region, Central Italy, August to October 2024
pmc-11583309.creator: Chiara Sacco, Augusto Liverani, Giulietta Venturi, Stefano Gavaudan, Flavia Riccardo, Giovanna Salvoni, Claudia Fortuna, Katia Marinelli, Giulia Marsili, Alessia Pesaresi, Carla Molina Grané, Irene Mercuri, Mattia Manica, Sara Caucci, Daniela Morelli, Lolita Sebastianelli, Maurilia Marcacci, Federic
pmc-11583309.description: Between August and 28 October 2024, 199 autochthonous cases of dengue virus serotype 2 were notified in the city of Fano, central Italy. We describe the ongoing epidemiological and microbiological investigation and public health measures implemented to contain the outbreak.

pmc-12398551.creator: Nchangwi Syntia Munung, Cornelius Ewuoso, Emile R Chimusa, Temidayo Ogundiran

pmc-12423084.title: Effect of Vitrectomy for Full-Thickness Macular Hole on Three-Dimensional Macular Shape
pmc-12423084.creator: Stewart Lake, Keryn Williams, Murk Bottema, Karen Reynolds
pmc-12423084.description: Purpose: To examine whether vitrectomy surgery for macular hole alters the 3-dimensional shape of the macula. Methods: Macular shape was measured on radially oriented spectral-domain optical coherence tomography scans centered on the fovea. Eyes of patients with a macular hole were imaged before and after surgical repair.

pmc-12665400.creator: Reo Hata, Shunsuke Funakoshi, Takeru Makiyama, Takao Kato, Megumi Narita, Yasuko Matsumura, Ryoko Hirohata, Yuki Naka, Kazumi Ida, Hiroaki Ito, Akihiko Yoshizawa, Yasuhito Nannya, Hironori Haga, Seishi Ogawa, Koh Ono, Takeshi Kimura, Yoshinori Yoshida
pmc-12665400.description: Visual AbstractKey Words: cardiac fibrosis, cardiac fibrosis organoid model, dilated cardiomyopathy, FGFR inhibition, transcriptomics Cardiac fibrosis, marked by excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix proteins in the myocardium, contributes significantly to various forms of cardiac dysfunction.1 In cardiomyopathy, this fibrosis often leads to irreversible cardiac impairment.

pmc-13404293.title: The readiness of primary healthcare facilities to address non-communicable diseases in rural Bangladesh
pmc-13404293.creator: Tanmoy Sarker, Wubin Xie, Ali Ahsan, Fahmida Akter, Md Mokbul Hossain, Aysha Anan, Jakia Sultana, Ian Goon, Fred Hersch, Zahidul Quayyum, Brian Oldenburg, John Chambers, Malay Kanti Mridha
pmc-13404293.description: IntroductionStrengthening the capacity of primary healthcare (PHC) systems is essential to address the rising burden of non-communicable diseases (NCD) in Bangladesh. The study assessed the readiness of rural PHC facilities in addressing the five World Health Organization (WHO) priority NCDs: diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, chronic respiratory diseases, cervical cancer, and mental health disorders.

pmc-13667317.title: Interventional Mitral Valve Edge‐to‐Edge Repair in Patients Above 85 Years of Age
pmc-13667317.creator: Florian Jürgens, Florian Schindhelm, Mohammed Abusharekh, Jürgen Kampf, Matthias Totzeck, Fadi Al‐Rashid, Peter Lüdike, Tienush Rassaf, Amir A. Mahabadi
pmc-13667317.description: BackgroundMitral valve transcatheter‐edge‐to‐edge repair (M‐TEER) is routinely performed in patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR) at high operative risk, frequently including elderly patients. Patients ≥ 85 years, however, are frequently excluded in clinical studies.ObjectivesWe evaluated differences of procedural characteristics and outcomes following M‐TEER in patients < versus ≥ 85 years.
